Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{QP}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{RQ}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{SQ}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{RT}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{TP}$ in terms of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$
worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $T$ to $P$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$ 

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{TP}=\overset{\to }{TR}+\overset{\to }{RQ}+\overset{\to }{QP}
$$

 

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/e0e6351dfbef6dadf6a6fb179f1545622ddaeab24c2c06dee03c87821304695c.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{TR}=-d,\,\overset{\to }{RQ}=b,\,\overset{\to }{QP}=a.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/02899ac9c536b0020514780db617e29977a5dc4daf60f42d80ed671883327fe3.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TP} & =\overset{\to }{TR}+\overset{\to }{RQ}+\overset{\to }{QP} \\  & =-d+b+a \\  & =a+b-d.\end{aligned}
$$
